note: Answers to questions people ask mid-emergency. Each card lists the ways people ask it, what we say back (12 words or fewer per line), and the source. `protocols` limits a card to those protocols (prefix match, so 'cpr' covers all three CPR protocols); empty means it applies anywhere. Ported and rewritten from the August 2026 prototype's cards (app/assets/knowledge/faq_2025.json).

ask: is it ok to move them
do i move them out of the road
say: Only move them if it's not safe where they are.
For CPR, flat on a firm floor is best.
cards.quote: Verify scene safety. [...] For adult cardiac arrest, rescuers should perform chest compressions with the patient on a firm surface and with the patient's torso at approximately the level of the rescuer's knees.

ask: is it safe to go in
is it safe to touch them
say: Check for traffic, fire, wires, or water first.
You can't help if you get hurt.
cards.quote: Verify scene safety.

ask: there is no one to help
say: Call 911 yourself, on speaker.
Put the phone down beside you and keep going.
cards.quote: Activate emergency response system.

say: About two inches deep. Let it come all the way up.
Follow the beat. It's set to the right speed.
cards.quote: During manual CPR, rescuers should perform chest compressions to a depth of at least 2 inches, or 5 cm, for an average adult while avoiding excessive chest compression depths (greater than 2.4 inches, or 6cm). [...] rescuers perform chest compressions at a rate of 100 to 120/min.

say: About a third of the depth of the chest.
Follow the beat. It's set to the right speed.
cards.note: Pediatric depth not yet confirmed against the 2025 pediatric text.

ask: where do i put my hands
say: Heel of one hand on the center of the chest.
Other hand on top. Arms straight.
cards.note: Hand position: confirm the 2025 Part 7 sentence.

ask: can i do cpr on a couch
should i move them to the floor
say: Get them flat on the floor. Not a bed.
cards.quote: For adult cardiac arrest, rescuers should perform chest compressions with the patient on a firm surface and with the patient's torso at approximately the level of the rescuer's knees.

ask: they are making a snoring noise
they took a breath should i stop
say: Gasping is not breathing.
Keep pushing.
cards.quote: The No-No-Go framework is reiterated as an effective method for recognizing OHCA.

ask: do i do mouth to mouth
do i have to put my mouth on theirs
say: If you're not trained, hands only is fine.
Just keep pushing.
cards.quote: they are to guide lay rescuers to use Hands-Only CPR for adults and conventional CPR, including breaths, for children.

ask: how long do i keep going
how long do i do this
say: Keep going until they breathe normally or paramedics take over.
Swap with someone every two minutes if you can.
cards.note: Continue until EMS takes over or signs of life; switch compressors about every 2 minutes. Confirm the 2025 Part 7 wording.

ask: how do i use the aed
how do i use a defibrillator
should i go get the aed
do i need to know how to use it
say: Turn it on. It talks you through every step.
Don't stop pushing to go look for one.
cards.quote: Early high-quality CPR and prompt defibrillation are the most important interventions associated with improved outcomes in adult cardiac arrest.

ask: do i have to take her bra off
do i take off the bra
say: You can move a bra aside.
No need to remove it.
cards.quote: When placing pads for defibrillation for an adult in cardiac arrest, it might be reasonable to adjust the position of a bra instead of removing it.

ask: should i hit them if they can cough
they can still breathe a little
say: If they can cough hard, let them cough.
Stay close and watch.
cards.quote: Encourage cough. Continue to check for signs of severe FBAO.

ask: i cannot get my arms around them
they are too big to reach around
say: Use chest thrusts instead of belly thrusts.
cards.quote: For patients in the late stages of pregnancy, or when the rescuer is unable to encircle the patient's abdomen, 5 chest thrusts should be used instead.

ask: it came out are they okay
do they still need a doctor
it is clear now what next
what now that it is out
say: Stay with them until help arrives.
Keep watching their breathing.
cards.quote: If object is expelled, continue to monitor until advanced care arrives.

ask: can i take the tourniquet off
say: Never loosen it. Only paramedics take it off.
It hurts because it's working.
cards.quote: Tourniquets HURT when applied effectively (they HURT A LOT) [...] Pain DOES NOT mean you should take the tourniquet off

ask: can i lift up to look
should i see if it stopped
say: Don't lift to check. Keep pressing until help arrives.
cards.quote: Don't release pressure to check the wound. [...] Hold pressure until relieved by medical responders.

ask: should i put ice on it
should i put butter on it
can i put cream on it
say: No ice, butter, or creams on it.
Cool running water only.
cards.quote: Do not apply oil, butter, ice, medicines, cream, oil spray, or any household remedy to a severe burn.

ask: how long do i run water
how long do i cool it
say: At least ten minutes. Twenty is better.
cards.quote: Begin immediate cooling of thermal burns, preferably with cool running water applied to the burn for a minimum of 10 minutes, ideally 20 minutes.

ask: what do i do about blisters
say: Don't pop blisters.
Cover it loosely with a clean cloth.
cards.quote: it may be reasonable to loosely cover a burn that has intact skin or an intact blister with a clean cloth or nonadherent dry dressing.

ask: how fast do they need help
say: Note when they last seemed normal.
Tell 911. Treatment depends on that time.
cards.quote: TIME: If a person shows any of these symptoms, time is essential. Call 911 or the local emergency number.

ask: when do i give another dose
say: No change in two to three minutes?
New spray, other nostril.
cards.quote: If they don't within 2-3 minutes, give a 2nd dose in the other nostril. You will need a new nasal spray for the 2nd dose.

ask: what if it is not opioids
i do not know what they took
say: Narcan won't hurt them if it isn't opioids.
Use it anyway.
cards.quote: If you think someone is having an overdose, use Narcan right away -- even if you don't know what drugs they took. Narcan only works for opioids, but there is no harm if they took a different drug.
